methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: After severe 76% electricity price hikes due to AI data centers, Virginia requires firms to pay for all dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure — state regulators crack down, governor says move will save civilians ‘hundreds of millions of dollars’ - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Severe electricity price hikes from data center infrastructure costs falling on residential ratepayers demonstrates how AI infrastructure concentration extracts value from communities without distributing capability or benefits, actively widening economic gaps.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional capacity-building outside NoVA that could develop regional AI fluency through hands-on learning, signaling distributed depth if the lab enables peer networks rather than remaining a siloed academic initiative.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free grassroots AI workshops explicitly targeting the technology gap in Hampton Roads demonstrates distributed skill-building through community networks, a core mechanism for broad fluency development outside traditional tech hubs.

signals.title: Fairfax Teen Builds Free AI Tool To Help Neurodivergent Job Seekers - Patch
signals.signal_reading: A Fairfax teen building accessible AI tools for neurodivergent job seekers signals youth-driven innovation and democratized capability, though remaining concentrated in NoVA suggests depth without yet achieving geographic distribution of peer learning networks.

signals.title: AI in Roanoke County schools: How new policies will guide student use - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke County schools developing AI use policies indicates platform-layer adoption spreading to rural districts, but policy focus over capability-building suggests shallow engagement where AI tools are consumed rather than deeply understood or created locally.
